note: Every edge case the desk is built to handle, with where it is checked. 'exam:' entries are cases in eval/cases/exam.json (a trailing * matches a numbered family); 'test:' entries are a test file and a phrase from a test name in it.

edge_cases.what: The same person written with a different spelling or script
edge_cases.expected: Escalate when birth date and nationality agree; close when they do not

edge_cases.what: Family name written first
edge_cases.expected: Treated as the same name; decided on the other fields

edge_cases.what: A first name given as an initial
edge_cases.expected: An initial stands for any name that starts with it

edge_cases.what: A title in front of a name
edge_cases.expected: The title is not part of the name

edge_cases.what: Accents added or removed
edge_cases.expected: Accents do not change the match

edge_cases.what: Hyphens and punctuation in names
edge_cases.expected: Punctuation does not change the match

edge_cases.what: Only a common surname is shared
edge_cases.expected: Close as a false positive when birth date and nationality differ

edge_cases.what: Look-alike Cyrillic or Greek letters inside a Latin name
edge_cases.expected: Seen through, flagged, and escalated like the real name

edge_cases.what: Legal-form words and spelling of a company name (Ltd, Limited, L.L.C.)
edge_cases.expected: Compared on the distinctive part of the name

edge_cases.what: A listed party with only a birth year, or a customer with no birth date
edge_cases.expected: Year-only conflicts close; a missing date asks for more information

edge_cases.what: Same name, clearly different birth date
edge_cases.expected: Close as a false positive when nationality also differs

edge_cases.what: A false positive for a customer who lives in a watched jurisdiction
edge_cases.expected: Policy sends it to a person anyway

edge_cases.what: A listed person owns exactly 50 percent
edge_cases.expected: Counts (at every level of a chain too); escalate

edge_cases.what: 49.9 percent
edge_cases.expected: Below the threshold; close

edge_cases.what: Two listed owners with 25 percent each
edge_cases.expected: They add up to 50; escalate (24 plus 25 stays below)

edge_cases.what: Ownership through holding companies
edge_cases.expected: A company owned 50 percent or more by blocked parties is itself blocked and its holdings count in full (the cascade); effective ownership, multiplied along the chain, is counted too

edge_cases.what: A chain longer than the policy allows
edge_cases.expected: Escalate; never guess

edge_cases.what: Companies that own each other
edge_cases.expected: The loop is reported and the check still finishes

edge_cases.what: The register gives no percentage
edge_cases.expected: Unknown, never zero; ask for more information

edge_cases.what: A listed entry changes after a case was cleared
edge_cases.expected: The clearance is stale; the case is re-opened

edge_cases.what: A listed party is removed from the list
edge_cases.expected: An escalation that rested on it becomes a candidate for release by a person

edge_cases.what: A new alert for a pair that was cleared before
edge_cases.expected: The earlier clearance is used as context if the entry is unchanged

edge_cases.what: Two decisions on the same customer and listed party disagree
edge_cases.expected: A person's later decision replaces the earlier one; the trust ledger records who overrode a decision and why
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/analyst-memory.test.ts::is replaced by a later decision of a person

edge_cases.what: A person overrides what memory says
edge_cases.expected: The override wins; the trust ledger records who overrode a decision and why

edge_cases.what: Zetaris is slow, down or returns nothing
edge_cases.expected: Held for a person: escalated at confidence 0 with held_reason data_service_unavailable; no record sealed; no invented decision

edge_cases.what: The payments service is down
edge_cases.expected: Payment alerts that need the payments table are held for a person (held_reason data_service_unavailable); customer alerts are unaffected

edge_cases.what: A model returns an empty answer, an error or invalid JSON
edge_cases.expected: One retry on the fast path, then a structured error; a critic that cannot answer approves nothing

edge_cases.what: The policy changes while a run is in progress
edge_cases.expected: The run keeps the version it started with
covered_by: test:apps/api/test/policy-and-events.test.ts::new policy version for runs started after a publish

edge_cases.what: The same alert is reviewed twice at once
edge_cases.expected: The second request is refused

edge_cases.what: Very long references and notes
edge_cases.expected: Cut to a fixed length in prompts, and said so

edge_cases.what: Instructions hidden in a name, note or payment reference
edge_cases.expected: Read as data, flagged, and never a reason to close

edge_cases.what: A draft that tells a customer they are being screened
edge_cases.expected: Refused

edge_cases.what: A policy change without a second approver
edge_cases.expected: Refused

edge_cases.what: A secret appears in a request or a model answer
edge_cases.expected: Redacted before anything is written

edge_cases.what: A listed person's address is in the customer's country, but the listed nationality differs. The country link must not be read as a nationality match. (A review step found this in a first version of the matcher, which counted an address country as nationality.)
edge_cases.expected: Only a possible match, never a strong one; the person decides, and the reason names the address-only link
covered_by: test:packages/data/test/compare.test.ts::tells a nationality match from an address-only country link

edge_cases.what: Payment to a beneficiary in a watched country, with a name that alone would not hold it
edge_cases.expected: Escalate; never close
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::payment routes that touch a watched jurisdiction

edge_cases.what: Beneficiary paid through a bank in a watched country
edge_cases.expected: Escalate; never close
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::payment routes that touch a watched jurisdiction

edge_cases.what: Payment routed through an intermediary bank in a watched country
edge_cases.expected: Escalate; never close
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::payment routes that touch a watched jurisdiction

edge_cases.what: The free-text reference names a watched country or place
edge_cases.expected: Escalate; whole words only, so "Iranian rugs" is not a hit
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::payment routes that touch a watched jurisdiction
test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::a place name that only contains a watched name

edge_cases.what: The same kind of payment with a clean route
edge_cases.expected: Not raised by the route rule
covered_by: test:packages/agents/test/policy-guard.test.ts::payment routes that stay clear of watched jurisdictions

edge_cases.what: The customer's name is a strong alias of the listed person, not the primary name
edge_cases.expected: Escalate when birth date and nationality agree

edge_cases.what: Same name and same birth date, but a different nationality and passport number
edge_cases.expected: Not closed as a false positive; a person decides

edge_cases.what: Birth date agrees but the nationality conflicts
edge_cases.expected: Escalate or ask for more information; never close
